Guidance
Rates and thresholds for employers 2026 to 2027
Use these rates and thresholds when you operate your payroll or provide expenses and benefits to your employees.

Print this page
Unless otherwise stated, the following figures apply from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027.
PAYE tax and Class 1 National Insurance contributions
You normally operate PAYE as part of your payroll so HMRC can collect Income Tax and National Insurance from your employees.
Your payroll software will work out how much tax and National Insurance to deduct from your employees’ pay. If you decide to run payroll yourself, you need to find payroll software to do this.
Tax thresholds, rates and codes
The amount of Income Tax you deduct from your employees depends on their tax code and how much of their taxable income is above their Personal Allowance .
England and Northern Ireland
The standard employee personal allowance for the 2026 to 2027 tax year is:
£242 per week
£1,048 per month
£12,570 per year
PAYE tax rate: Basic tax rate; Rate of tax: 20%; Annual earnings the rate applies to (above the PAYE threshold): Up to £37,700
PAYE tax rate: Higher tax rate; Rate of tax: 40%; Annual earnings the rate applies to (above the PAYE threshold): From £37,701 to £125,140
PAYE tax rate: Additional tax rate; Rate of tax: 45%; Annual earnings the rate applies to (above the PAYE threshold): Above £125,140
Scotland
The standard employee personal allowance for the 2026 to 2027 tax year is:
£242 per week
£1,048 per month
£12,570 per year
PAYE tax rate: Starter tax rate; Rate of tax: 19%; Annual earnings the rate applies to (above the PAYE threshold): Up to £3,967
PAYE tax rate: Basic tax rate; Rate of tax: 20%; Annual earnings the rate applies to (above the PAYE threshold): From £3,968 to £16,956
PAYE tax rate: Intermediate tax rate; Rate of tax: 21%; Annual earnings the rate applies to (above the PAYE threshold): From £16,957 to £31,092
PAYE tax rate: Higher tax rate; Rate of tax: 42%; Annual earnings the rate applies to (above the PAYE threshold): From £31,093 to £62,430
PAYE tax rate: Advanced tax rate; Rate of tax: 45%; Annual earnings the rate applies to (above the PAYE threshold): From £62,431 to £125,140
PAYE tax rate: Top tax rate; Rate of tax: 48%; Annual earnings the rate applies to (above the PAYE threshold): Above £125,140
Wales
The standard employee personal allowance for the 2026 to 2027 tax year is:
£242 per week
£1,048 per month
£12,570 per year
PAYE tax rate: Basic tax rate; Rate of tax: 20%; Annual earnings the rate applies to (above the PAYE threshold): Up to £37,700
PAYE tax rate: Higher tax rate; Rate of tax: 40%; Annual earnings the rate applies to (above the PAYE threshold): From £37,701 to £125,140
PAYE tax rate: Additional tax rate; Rate of tax: 45%; Annual earnings the rate applies to (above the PAYE threshold): Above £125,140
Emergency tax codes
The emergency tax codes from 6 April 2026 are:
1257L W1
1257L M1
1257L X
Find out more about emergency tax codes .
Class 1 National Insurance thresholds
Class 1 National Insurance thresholds: Lower earnings limit; 2026 to 2027: £129 per week £559 per month £6,708 per year
Class 1 National Insurance thresholds: Primary threshold; 2026 to 2027: £242 per week £1,048 per month £12,570 per year
Class 1 National Insurance thresholds: Secondary threshold; 2026 to 2027: £96 per week £417 per month £5,000 per year
Class 1 National Insurance thresholds: Freeport upper secondary threshold; 2026 to 2027: £481 per week £2,083 per month £25,000 per year
Class 1 National Insurance thresholds: Investment Zone upper secondary threshold; 2026 to 2027: £481 per week £2,083 per month £25,000 per year
Class 1 National Insurance thresholds: Upper secondary threshold (under 21); 2026 to 2027: £967 per week £4,189 per month £50,270 per year
Class 1 National Insurance thresholds: Apprentice upper secondary threshold (apprentice under 25); 2026 to 2027: £967 per week £4,189 per month £50,270 per year
Class 1 National Insurance thresholds: Veterans upper secondary threshold; 2026 to 2027: £967 per week £4,189 per month £50,270 per year
Class 1 National Insurance thresholds: Upper earnings limit; 2026 to 2027: £967 per week £4,189 per month £50,270 per year
Class 1 National Insurance rates
Employee (primary) contribution rates
Deduct primary contributions (employee’s National Insurance) from your employees’ pay through PAYE .
National Insurance category letter: A; Earnings at or above lower earnings limit up to and including primary threshold: 0%; Earnings above primary threshold up to and including upper earnings limit: 8%; Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit: 2%
National Insurance category letter: B; Earnings at or above lower earnings limit up to and including primary threshold: 0%; Earnings above primary threshold up to and including upper earnings limit: 1.85%; Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit: 2%
National Insurance category letter: C; Earnings at or above lower earnings limit up to and including primary threshold: nil; Earnings above primary threshold up to and including upper earnings limit: nil; Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit: nil
National Insurance category letter: D (Investment Zone — deferment); Earnings at or above lower earnings limit up to and including primary threshold: 0%; Earnings above primary threshold up to and including upper earnings limit: 2%; Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit: 2%
National Insurance category letter: E (Investment Zone — married women and widows reduced rate); Earnings at or above lower earnings limit up to and including primary threshold: 0%; Earnings above primary threshold up to and including upper earnings limit: 1.85%; Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit: 2%
National Insurance category letter: F (Freeport); Earnings at or above lower earnings limit up to and including primary threshold: 0%; Earnings above primary threshold up to and including upper earnings limit: 8%; Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit: 2%
National Insurance category letter: H (apprentice under 25); Earnings at or above lower earnings limit up to and including primary threshold: 0%; Earnings above primary threshold up to and including upper earnings limit: 8%; Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit: 2%
National Insurance category letter: I (Freeport — married women and widows reduced rate); Earnings at or above lower earnings limit up to and including primary threshold: 0%; Earnings above primary threshold up to and including upper earnings limit: 1.85%; Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit: 2%
National Insurance category letter: J; Earnings at or above lower earnings limit up to and including primary threshold: 0%; Earnings above primary threshold up to and including upper earnings limit: 2%; Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit: 2%
National Insurance category letter: K (Investment Zone — state pensioner); Earnings at or above lower earnings limit up to and including primary threshold: nil; Earnings above primary threshold up to and including upper earnings limit: nil; Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit: nil
National Insurance category letter: L (Freeport — deferment); Earnings at or above lower earnings limit up to and including primary threshold: 0%; Earnings above primary threshold up to and including upper earnings limit: 2%; Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit: 2%
National Insurance category letter: M (under 21); Earnings at or above lower earnings limit up to and including primary threshold: 0%; Earnings above primary threshold up to and including upper earnings limit: 8%; Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit: 2%
National Insurance category letter: N (Investment Zone); Earnings at or above lower earnings limit up to and including primary threshold: 0%; Earnings above primary threshold up to and including upper earnings limit: 8%; Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit: 2%
National Insurance category letter: S (Freeport — state pensioner); Earnings at or above lower earnings limit up to and including primary threshold: nil; Earnings above primary threshold up to and including upper earnings limit: nil; Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit: nil
National Insurance category letter: V (veteran); Earnings at or above lower earnings limit up to and including primary threshold: 0%; Earnings above primary threshold up to and including upper earnings limit: 8%; Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit: 2%
National Insurance category letter: Z (under 21 — deferment); Earnings at or above lower earnings limit up to and including primary threshold: 0%; Earnings above primary threshold up to and including upper earnings limit: 2%; Balance of earnings above upper earnings limit: 2%
Employer (secondary) contribution rates
You pay secondary contributions (employer’s National Insurance) to HMRC as part of your PAYE bill.
Find out more about running payroll and paying HMRC and how to Pay employers’ PAYE tax and National Insurance .

Director’s contribution rates
The rates also apply to directors. You can read more information about:
the methods used for working out National Insurance contributions for company directors
the rules for paying National Insurance contributions for company directors
Class 1A National Insurance: expenses and benefits
You must pay Class 1A National Insurance on work benefits you give to your employees, for example a company mobile phone. You report and pay Class 1A on expenses and benefits at the end of each tax year.
The National Insurance Class 1A rate on expenses and benefits for 2026 to 2027 is 15%.
Find out more about expenses and benefits for employers .
Class 1A National Insurance: termination awards and sporting testimonial payments
Class 1A National Insurance contributions are due on the amount of termination awards paid to employees which are over £30,000 and on the amount of sporting testimonial payments paid by independent committees which are over £100,000. You report and pay Class 1A on these types of payments during the tax year as part of your payroll.
The National Insurance Class 1A rate on termination awards and sporting testimonial payments for 2026 to 2027 is 15%.
Pay employers’ Class 1A National Insurance .
Class 1B National Insurance: PAYE Settlement Agreements ( PSAs )
You pay Class 1B National Insurance if you have a PAYE Settlement Agreement . This allows you to make one annual payment to cover all the tax and National Insurance due on small or irregular taxable expenses or benefits for your employees.
The National Insurance Class 1B rate for 2026 to 2027 is 15%.
Pay Class 1B National Insurance .
